subject: PO entity billing, pricing slab reconciliation, and net-term options
messages:
From: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@skybridgehealth.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@skybridgehealth.com
Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on PO format, invoice cadence and discount slabs

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the team liked the performance numbers and the dedicated capacity option for our analytics workloads. Procurement has a couple of constraints before we can move the PO forward and wanted to confirm Redwood's approach so we can map it to our ERP.

1) PO fields: our AP system requires a single blanket PO number that can be referenced across three legal billing entities. We typically ask vendors to accept an additional PO line that indicates the billing entity code per invoice. Can Redwood accept a blanket PO with "billing-entity" line-level mapping or do you require separate POs per entity?

2) Invoice cadence: preferred is consolidated monthly invoices (one PDF with entity breakdown) but in some states our tax team requires an invoice per legal entity. What flexibility do you offer for per-entity vs consolidated invoicing?

3) Net terms & discounts: budget prefers Net60 for split-entity billing. You've presented tiered discounts based on committed spend. If we move to Net60 (no prepay), what happens to the volume discount tiers? Would the discount stack be the same as Net45/Net30 options?

I attached an example of our PO format for reference (SkyBridge_PO_Example.pdf). Can you confirm what fields you need to populate correctly?

Best,
Elena Martinez
Senior Procurement Manager
SkyBridge Health

Attachments: SkyBridge_PO_Example.pdf (pdf)

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@skybridgehealth.com>
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on PO format, invoice cadence and discount slabs

Elena — thanks for the clear summary and for the sample PO. Forwarding to operations and finance so we can give concrete options. Quick answers up front:

- Blanket PO: we can accept a single blanket PO referencing multiple billing entities. Our AR system prefers an explicit "billing_entity" field on each invoice line (we map that to your ERP codes). So the PO is fine if you can provide the entity code on each usage line or in an attached mapping file.

- Invoice cadence: we support both consolidated monthly invoices with per-entity line breakdowns (single PDF) and separate PDFs per legal entity. The consolidated invoice is the default for committed customers. Separate PDFs add an operational overhead fee unless tied to a contractual commitment.

- Net terms & discounts: standard hosted pricing assumes Net45. For Net60 we typically adjust the discount slabs downward slightly to cover credit exposure unless there is an annual commit/advance. I attached our current slab sheet (Redwood_pricing_slabs.xlsx) with example calculations.

Next steps: Vanessa (ops) and Karthik (billing) are looped for the technical PO/ERP mapping and exact discount math. If you can indicate which of the three options you prefer (A: consolidated monthly net45 with 12-month commit; B: consolidated monthly net60 w/ reduced slab; C: split-entity monthly net60 with per-entity invoice fee), we'll run exact numbers and return a proposal.

Jonas — thanks for the quick reply. A couple of clarifying questions from our side (finance leads on copy below):

• Blanket PO mapping: we can provide a small CSV mapping file that contains PO line -> billing_entity_code. Is that sufficient for Redwood to generate line-level entity tags for ERP? If yes, what column headers are required?

• Fee for per-entity PDFs: can you quantify the operational fee if we must receive separate PDFs per entity (our tax compliance team is pushing for that in CA and MA)? Is the fee per invoice or a monthly uplift?

• Discount slab example: can you show a concrete example where an annualized committed spend of $1.2M across three entities (split 50/30/20) maps to your tiered discount under options A/B/C from your note? We need the net spend after discount to circulate to procurement and FP&A.

We're attaching the PO example again and will aim to confirm preferred option by early next week.

Regards,
SkyBridge Procurement

Attachments: SkyBridge_PO_Example.pdf (pdf)

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: SkyBridge Procurement <procurement@skybridgehealth.com>, Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@skybridgehealth.com>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 10 Jul 2026 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on PO format, invoice cadence and discount slabs

Hi Elena / team — Vanessa from Finance Ops here. Appreciate the PO example. Answers and a proposal below.

1) CSV mapping: yes — we can consume a CSV with headers: po_number, line_number, billing_entity_code, sku_code, quantity, unit_price, start_date, end_date. If your CSV uses different headers we can map on ingest but the above reduces manual work.

2) Per-entity PDF fee: if separate PDFs are required, we charge a $250 monthly operational fee (not per invoice) to cover segregation, departmental tax stamping, and manual validation. If you opt for a contract amendment that includes a 12-month commitment and consolidated invoicing, we waive the fee.

3) Discount math (example): using the attached slab sheet:
- Scenario: $1.2M annualized total across entities (E1 50% = $600k, E2 30% = $360k, E3 20% = $240k)
- Option A (consolidated w/ 12-mo commit, Net45): aggregate tiers hit higher slabs -> blended discount = 12% -> net spend = $1,056,000
- Option B (consolidated w/o commit, Net60): lower slab by ~2 percentage points -> blended discount = 10% -> net spend = $1,080,000
- Option C (split entities, Net60): tiers applied per-entity -> blended discount = 9% -> net spend = $1,092,000 plus $250 monthly per-entity fee (waivable with 12-mo commit)

Operational asks: we will need the CSV mapping at time of first invoice and your ERP billing codes for each legal entity. We can produce either a consolidated invoice PDF with entity sections (recommended) or three PDFs if required.

Draft amendment: I'll prepare a short amendment that captures the selected option and any waivers on per-entity fees. If you confirm Option A/Option B/C preference, we'll turn around a DocuSign link and a clean pricing exhibit.

Vanessa / Jonas — this is helpful, thanks. We discussed with FP&A and legal; we are inclined to accept Option B (consolidated monthly invoices, Net60, reduced slab) if Redwood can guarantee:

• A pricing exhibit that shows the slab math and final net monthly invoice examples (our FP&A needs line-by-line).
• A commitment to provide the CSV mapping at first invoice and a one-time onboarding call to validate the mapping.

If you can generate the amendment and a DocuSign link with Option B + pricing exhibit, we'll push this through our internal signature process.

Please also include a HubSpot deal id or internal contract id in the DocuSign so our AP team can reconcile once the PO is live (our system requires the vendor contract id on invoices).

Thanks — target to sign this week if we get the DocuSign and exhibit.
